heroHeadline: 15 Airstrikes Hit Mindat in Single Day; KIA Advances in Sagaing as Junta Loses Grip on Stronghold; BROUK Documents AA Sexual Violence Against Rohingya; 30,900+ Displaced in Kani, Sagaing
heroSubtitle: On Day 1,929 of Myanmar's civil war (May 15, 2026), the Myanmar junta escalated its post-Falam Chin Hills offensive with approximately 15 coordinated airstrikes on Mindat and Kanpetlet towns in southern Chin State in a single day — killing 4 including a prisoner of war, confirmed by the Chin People's Union and Army (CPU/A) — following 11 strikes over May 13-14. The Chin bombing campaign is one dimension of a coordinated multi-front SAC offensive that has also seen a large-scale ground assault with 20+ airstrikes across Pauk, Saw, and Kyaukhtu townships in Magway Region (May 13-14), and an ongoing SAC campaign in Kani Township, Sagaing that has displaced 30,900+ civilians from 44 villages. On the resistance side, the Irrawaddy reported that KIA-led forces are advancing on a key Sagaing stronghold as a counter-offensive to the junta's May 5 Mawlu recapture — with the AA simultaneously pressing an offensive against SAC Artillery Battalion 344 in Ayeyarwady Region to cut junta supply routes into southern Rakhine. A major human rights development emerged on May 15 as the Burmese Rohingya Organisation UK (BROUK) documented systematic sexual violence — rape, gang rape, arbitrary detention, and forced recruitment — against Rohingya women and girls by Arakan Army forces in northern Rakhine State, raising urgent concerns about the treatment of the 600,000+ Rohingya remaining in Myanmar under AA governance. The US confirmed it is reviewing a proposal to transfer $1 billion in frozen Myanmar funds for non-lethal aid to revolutionary forces.
footerNote: Data sourced from AAPP, ACLED, UN OCHA, Irrawaddy, RFA, Myanmar Now, DVB, Al Jazeera, Mizzima, Human Rights Watch, Crisis Group, Myanmar Peace Monitor, MoeMaKa CDM News, IMNA / Mon News Agency, CPJ, Narinjara News, Global Arakan Network, Kachin Human Rights Watch, Aryan Age, NUG Ministry of Human Rights, Committee to Protect Journalists, Chin People's Union and Army (CPU/A), Burmese Rohingya Organisation UK (BROUK), and official NUG, KNU, KIA, AA, and PDF statements.
